Synopsis:
Escalating attacks on commercial vessels and port infrastructure in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov are severely disrupting grain exports from Russia (world's largest exporter) and Ukraine (5th largest). Casualties among seafarers are rising sharply. Russian grain exports reportedly fell to ~40% of normal capacity in August; Ukraine exported only ~1/3 of potential volumes. This is compounding existing food supply pressures — including the Iran conflict, poor European harvests, and El Niño — and is forecast to drive global food prices up ~12% this year and a further ~4.8% in 2027.
